    id,
    status,
    case status
        when 'completed' then 'done'
        when 'shipped' then 'on the way'

from jaffle_shop.orders
where id in (1, 7, 8, 9, 290)
order by id;

examples.chapterTitle: SQL from Zero to Exam Level
examples.bookSql:
-- GROUP BY ALL: group by every column that is not an aggregate
select paymentmethod, status, count(*) as n
from stripe.payments
group by all
order by paymentmethod, status;

-- FILTER: an aggregate that only looks at some rows
select
    count(*) as all_payments,
    count(*) filter (where status = 'fail') as failed,
    sum(case when status = 'fail' then 1 else 0 end) as failed_portable
from stripe.payments;

    select
        id as order_id,
        user_id as customer_id
    from jaffle_shop.orders

examples.title: queries/customer_orders.sql
examples.bookSql:
with

-- 1. import CTEs: one per raw table, only the columns we need
customers as (
    select
        id as customer_id,
        first_name,
        last_name
    from jaffle_shop.customers
),

orders as (
    select
        id as order_id,
        user_id as customer_id,
        order_date
    from jaffle_shop.orders
),

payments as (
    select
        orderid as order_id,
        status,
        amount
    from stripe.payments
),

-- 2. logical CTEs: one business step each
order_payments as (
    select
        order_id,
        sum(amount) as amount_cents
    from payments
    where status = 'success'
    group by order_id
),

customer_orders as (
    select
        customer_id,
        min(order_date) as first_order_date,
        max(order_date) as most_recent_order_date,
        count(order_id) as number_of_orders
    from orders
    group by customer_id
),

customer_payments as (
    select
        orders.customer_id,
        sum(order_payments.amount_cents) as lifetime_value_cents
    from orders
    inner join order_payments
        on orders.order_id = order_payments.order_id
    group by orders.customer_id
),

-- 3. final CTE: one row per customer
final as (
    select
        customers.customer_id,
        customers.first_name,
        customers.last_name,
        customer_orders.first_order_date,
        customer_orders.most_recent_order_date,
        coalesce(customer_orders.number_of_orders, 0) as number_of_orders,
        coalesce(customer_payments.lifetime_value_cents, 0) / 100
            as lifetime_value
    from customers
    left join customer_orders
        on customers.customer_id = customer_orders.customer_id
    left join customer_payments
        on customers.customer_id = customer_payments.customer_id
)

select * from final
order by customer_id

examples.chapterTitle: Data Tests
examples.title: target/compiled/.../accepted_values_stg_jaffle_sho_ae65ba2c55b7467c3aa7315d19f96acd.sql
examples.bookSql:
with all_values as (

    select
        status as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from "practice"."dbt_adnane"."stg_jaffle_shop__orders"
    group by status

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    'placed','shipped','completed'
)

examples.annotation: The book shows the dbt log "FAIL 2": a failing test is a query that returns rows, so the check is "this query returns 2 rows". The model stg_jaffle_shop__orders is compiled from the reference project (same file at tags ch11 and ch18) and created as a view in the browser.
